text:
Alex C (customer): Hey support — hitting a hard error from the ranking endpoint when we send ~600 docs. Response is just '413 Payload Too Large' with no detail. Can you advise? We need to know whether to trim docs or queries.

Maria S: Sorry you're blocked, Alex. Can you paste the request body (or a redacted version) and the exact HTTP response body+headers? Also which region and API key (prod/test) you used.

Alex C (customer): Repro below (redacted keys). Note we already chunked docs, but each doc is ~800-1,200 chars. cURL:```bash
curl -X POST \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/ranker\" \\ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \\ 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\ 
  -d '{\"query\":\"How to reset password?\",\"documents\":[\"<doc1 long text>\",\"<doc2>\"/* 600 entries */]}'
```
Response: HTTP/1.1 413 Payload Too Large
Body: {"error":"payload_too_large"}
Headers: x-request-id: r-abc123

Maria S: Thanks. That body is not actionable. I can tell them to reduce documents but we need precise limits to give the customer. Escalating to eng. @Devin K can you check what we validate server-side and whether errors can be more specific (e.g., which doc blew the token budget, or total tokens vs max_docs)?

support-bot: New escalation created: INFR-1234 (priority: P2)

Devin K: Thanks for the ping. Quick summary: the ranker currently enforces two guards — max_documents (300 per request) and token_budget (combined tokens of query+docs, 8192 default). The request short-circuits in the HTTP parser when body size > 10MB, which returns 413 without JSON detail. So customers sending many medium-long docs can hit body-size limit before we compute tokens.

Maria S: Ah — so sometimes the 413 originates from HTTP layer (size) not the logical rerank token limit. That explains ambiguity. Can we detect and return a friendlier message? Customer-facing should say whether docs count, token budget, or raw body size was exceeded.

Devin K: Agreed. Proposed actions:
1) Short-term (hotfix): intercept 413 at ingress and attempt to parse Content-Length / size to return JSON like:
```json
{\"error\":\"request_too_large\",\"reason\":\"raw_payload_size_exceeded\",\"max_bytes\":10485760}
```
2) Mid-term: add a pre-parse pass to count array lengths (documents) and return a 400 with structured error if docs > max_documents. Also return detailed token summary when token budget exceeded: `{"error":"tokens_exceeded","max_tokens":8192,"estimated_tokens":15324,"query_tokens":24,"docs_tokens":15300}`
3) Docs/SDK: update support KB and SDK client to surface these errors clearly and give automatic truncation helpers.

Samir P: +1 on that plan. From product POV we should also consider raising the default max_documents for Dedicated customers or allowing a flag to accept streamed docs. For hosted, better error messages first.

Maria S: For the immediate customer reply, I drafted a canned message: "We hit an HTTP payload size limit — please try sending fewer documents or compressing text. If you're under 10MB and still get this, please paste the raw response headers so we can check token budget." Thoughts?

Jordan L: I'll update the KB once engineering confirms the field names in the error JSON. Can we have a reproducible script for QA to validate both body-size and token-budget errors? I can own the QA ticket.

Devin K: I'll push a small change to ingress to convert raw 413 into a structured JSON if Content-Length > max_bytes. I'll open a PR today: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFR-1234. Expect a canary deploy in 48h. For token accounting errors, that's a separate PR that needs more careful handling — ETA 1 week.

Alex C (customer): Appreciate the quick follow-up. One question: would you consider returning which document index caused the token blowup? That would save us trial-and-error.

Devin K: We can include `largest_doc_index` in the tokens_exceeded error when we compute tokens — but note when body > 10MB we never compute tokens. That's why the first fix is important.

Maria S: Taking notes for the customer. I'll reply with the interim guidance and ask them to check Content-Length header. Also offering to accept a sample payload via secure upload for us to repro.

Alex C (customer): Uploaded a sanitized sample to the secure dropbox you shared. Let me know once you can repro.

Samir P: Action items:
- Devin: ingress hotfix to return structured 413 (48h).
- Devin: token-accounting error JSON (1w).
- Jordan: QA scripts for both cases (3d).
- Maria: customer update and intake of sanitized payload (today).
- Samir: review product settings for default limits for Dedicated (next sprint).

Maria S: Thanks team — I'll send the customer the interim reply and mark the thread as escalated. :thumbsup:

support-bot: Escalation INFR-1234 updated: assignee=Devin K, status=In Progress

Devin K: quick note for engs reproducing locally: example script to hit body-size 413:```bash
python3 -c \"import json; d={'query':'x','documents':['a'*1200]*600}; print(len(json.dumps(d).encode()))\" # should be > 10MB
curl -X POST 'https://localhost:8443/v1/ranker' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @payload.json -v
```

Jordan L: adding QA checklist to the ticket and will add tests to CI for both error shapes.

Maria S: Closing loop with customer now. Will ping here if they still see problems after the ingress fix. :eyes:
